decisions.baseline_policy: Retain declared WLC provisionally, not a demonstrated historical victory. No note-only substitution for the held full candidate.

rationale.attestation: De Rossi explicitly reports וישתבחו in Hebrew copies. His page258 also reports וישתכחו marginal qere in Kennicott553/DeRossi331. These facts establish qualified published bet attestation, not an independent manuscript count, ancient copy date or fresh glyph discovery.
rationale.bet_best_case: Greek passive praise is genuinely different from forgetting, and published Hebrew bet reports make a Hebrew praise/boast-source hypothesis serious.8:11-14 supply coherent injustice/delayed-punishment context. A rarer praise root becoming a common forget root is possible, but the conversion direction is not observed.
rationale.bet_countercase: Late Hebrew bet copies may reflect reception or corrections. Gittin's alternate-reading formula supports a homiletic interpretation, not a continuous Hebrew bet text. Greek may reflect a different source or interpretation; Latin and multiple Greek editions are not independent Hebrew votes. No dated identified direct Hebrew target presently resolves the direction.
rationale.kaf_best_case: Selected WLC and reported Syriac/Targum express forgetting; Hebrew book controls2:16/9:5 explicitly place forgetting after death. The reading is contextually possible rather than automatically corrupt.
rationale.kaf_countercase: The praise version and direct published bet reports cannot be dismissed as an unattested conjecture. Immediate delayed-punishment context makes praise or self-commendation attractive. Retaining WLC does not resolve the priority question.
rationale.chronology: Earlier Greek praise reporting increases interest in the bet-source hypothesis, but its translation date, physical copy dates and exact Hebrew inference must remain separate. Removing this chronological advantage weakens bet's historical case; it does not eliminate its published Hebrew attestation. With it, priority still remains unresolved.
rationale.english_reflexive_vs_passive: Had boasted is a plausible reflexive interpretation supported by the Hebrew Psalm/Chronicles controls. It changes agency from receiving public praise to self-commendation and must not borrow Greek passive praise as direct support for that agency. Hitpael is not uniformly reflexive; a passive analysis cannot be ruled out by the stem label alone.
rationale.english_bet_scope: The controls' ב introduces the object of glorying, but בעיר can be locative. The exact candidate does not need to mean boasting about the city, and no grammatical rule here requires rejecting an absolute boast plus location. Those two closely related controls do not establish the target's local sense by themselves.
rationale.english_timing_subject: Had boasted makes the activity anterior to seeing the wicked buried, consistent with its inherited had come and gone clause. It avoids dead people boasting and is intelligible English. The Hebrew perfect/imperfect sequence does not uniquely mark that pluperfect relation or settle whether all plural verbs share the wicked subject. The candidate is possible, not established as the optimal reading.
rationale.english_literary_effect: Prior boasting could illustrate impunity and lead into8:11, but removes the public/postmortem approval effect of passive praise. Where they had done so leaves the referent of so compressed; it does not prove a temple-flaunting narrative or justify importing righteous works. Burial/coming/going ambiguity needs a whole-clause argument, not merely a changed target lexeme.
rationale.mechanical: Exact composition accounts for one kaf-to-bet word change; proposal-only schema, original revision preservation, archived metadata and target reader notes pass focused checks. Baseline revised status fails the present draft-only schema as recorded. None of these checks establishes historical priority or permits production schema changes.
